name: execute_command
description: Start a shell command. Destructive, privilege-escalation, remote-shell, and network-listener commands are blocked; ordinary HTTP clients and package managers are allowed. Truncated output reports shown/total counts; narrow or page instead of rerunning variants. Failures report the exit code. For long-running commands, start with `yield_time_ms` and control the returned session with `command_session`.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later execute_command calls in this turn:
- Long-running or interactive commands: start with `yield_time_ms`, then use `command_session` with action=poll/write/close and the returned session id. Prefer this over `&` plus log-file polling.
- `sleep` is expensive: it blocks the whole turn on dead time — do not use it unless truly necessary (e.g. waiting for a server to accept connections). Prefer `command_session` polling for commands already running, or `task_wait` for subagent tasks.

command.description: Shell command to start. Long-running or interactive work should use `yield_time_ms` instead of relying on the 60-300s one-shot timeout. Do not pipe interactive commands through `head`, `tail`, `grep`, or `tee`; they can wait for process exit and stall.

input.description: Optional text written verbatim to the command's stdin immediately after spawn, up to 16 KiB. Include a trailing newline for line-oriented prompts. Omit when not needed; an empty string means no input. For pty=true this is typed into the terminal: closing the writer does not send EOF, so a program that reads until EOF will wait for timeout; send `\u0004` (Ctrl-D) explicitly for that case. Do not send secrets; the text becomes part of the tool call history.

pty.description: Required: always supply this field (the call is rejected if omitted). Use true only for interactive CLIs (prompts, QR codes, full-screen UI); use false for everything else, including background commands. With `yield_time_ms`, `pty=true` starts a persistent PTY session controlled through `command_session`.

yield_time_ms.description: Start a persistent command session and wait up to this many milliseconds for output (1-30000, default 10000). Returns a session id when the process is still running; control it with `command_session`. Use this for long builds, REPLs, and multi-step interactive commands.
